papers.title: Narrow Multimodal Fine-Tuning Can Induce Emergent Misalignment
papers.problem: Teams fine-tune vision-language models on narrow tasks, but nobody knew if that makes them misbehave elsewhere.
papers.fix: Narrow fine-tuning caused broad harmful behavior in fifteen vision-language models, including unsafe images, dishonesty, and risky agent actions.
papers.practicalUseCase: A model tuned for one small job can turn unsafe everywhere, so test it on unrelated tasks before shipping.
papers.limitation: Prompt tricks, extra benign training, and steering only partly reduced the harm.

papers.title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
papers.problem: Vision-language models fail at spatial, physical, and time-based reasoning, and no shared training data targeted the cause.
papers.fix: A 36,076-example dataset called WOVEN lifted 22 of 26 outside tests, by up to 27.3 percentage points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If your model misjudges how scenes change, train it on state-change examples chosen by reasoning type.
papers.limitation: The authors tested this on benchmarks, and the strongest of 38 models still fell far below humans.

papers.title: HyperThink: Text-to-Parameter Hypernetworks for Efficient Reasoning
papers.problem: Long thinking traces make language models answer well but slowly, because the model writes every step one by one.
papers.fix: HyperThink predicts a small model update from the question, so the model skips thinking traces and uses far fewer tokens.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you need fast answers on math or logic, this trades long reasoning for lower delay with little accuracy loss.
papers.limitation: Gains were strongest when the model barely thinks, and the tests covered math and general reasoning only.

papers.title: PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.problem: Agents trained with one reward per episode learn slowly, and token-level hints from a skill miss most of its effect.
papers.fix: PR-OPD aligns hidden states with a skill-aware teacher, beating GRPO by up to 4.7 (ALFWorld) and 14.0 (WebShop) points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train web or home agents, copy the skill's effect inside the model, not only in its word probabilities.
papers.limitation: Results come from two test environments and two model backbones, so other agent tasks remain untested.

papers.title: UNITAS: A 3D-Native World Action Model for Embodied Manipulation
papers.problem: Robot models built on image generators miss real distances, because images only show flat views of a 3D world.
papers.fix: UNITAS works in 3D space and reached 99.8% on LIBERO and 85% average across real-world tasks, with 1.7B parameters.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build robot arms, plan motion in measured 3D space, not pixels, to cut errors by up to 49%.
papers.limitation: The 49% error cut compares only against selected methods on RoboTwin, not every robot model.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk grew fast, but nobody had mapped how it grew or what sets the size of each issue.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk issues, equity-based contracts, strong security, longer debt, and USD or Euro denomination raised issue size.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you track green sukuk, expect big issues from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, and from equity-based deals.
papers.limitation: Sustainability sukuk stay a tiny share of all sukuk, and the data stops at 2022.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked proof that artificial intelligence and big data actually improve their competitiveness and sustainability.
papers.fix: A survey of 214 managers linked AI, big data skills, and data management to higher competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run a bank, invest in AI and data systems, because staff digital skill alone did not help sustainability.
papers.limitation: The survey covers one country at one point in time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual systems lacked clear evidence on which digital and national factors drive their growth.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, technology adoption was the strongest driver of bank growth.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan bank growth, fund digital systems first, since high-tech exports only help when paired with technology adoption.
papers.limitation: The sample covers 12 countries, and institutional quality only helped growth indirectly.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Financial inclusion stays low in many Muslim countries, even though Islamic finance expanded over the past decade.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, tertiary education, institution quality, and internet access drive inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you design inclusion policy for OIC countries, invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women, and income growth first.
papers.limitation: The study compares country-level averages, so it cannot show what works inside one bank or region.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks form sustainability committees, but it was unclear whether those committees produce real environmental action.
papers.fix: Committees raised environmental scores in all four areas at conventional banks, but Islamic banks improved only overall and resource scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you judge a bank's green claims, check for real products and innovations, not just committee presence.
papers.limitation: The data comes from emerging-market banks with both bank types, and shows links rather than cause.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and peer comparison, which may make them feel like frauds despite real achievement.
papers.fix: Impostor phenomenon was frequent among medical students worldwide, though results varied a lot by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud while training, know that many peers do too, so talk about it.
papers.limitation: Studies differed widely, so the pooled rate is rough and the paper tested no fixes.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI heavily, but experts did not know what drives their new research ideas.
papers.fix: Both inner drive and outside rewards push doctoral students toward innovation, and they work together instead of competing.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you do research, keep your basic needs met, since long low motivation cuts your flexibility and willingness to explore.
papers.limitation: Data came from one-time self-reported surveys in chemistry, so bias is possible and change over time is unseen.
